review_note: Pinned lemma 761 states affine Spec(R) Jacobson iff R Jacobson. Stage A adds explicit X=Spec R but keeps the two-way correspondence.
statement:
An affine scheme $\Spec(R)$ is Jacobson if and only if
the ring $R$ is Jacobson.
conclusions: $X$ is a Jacobson scheme if and only if $R$ is a Jacobson ring.

review_note: Pinned lemma 775 states five equivalent scheme-Jacobson conditions (global, locally-P, every affine ring, existence of affine cover, existence of open cover) and inheritance by open subschemes. The precise scopes remain.
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scheme $X$ is Jacobson.
\item The scheme $X$ is ``locally Jacobson'' in the sense of
Definition \ref{definition-locally-P}.
\item For every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$
is Jacobson.
\item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ such that
each $\mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is Jacobson.
\item There exists an open covering $X = \bigcup X_j$
such that each open subscheme $X_j$ is Jacobson.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $X$ is Jacobson then every open subscheme
is Jacobson.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locally-jacobson}
Let $X$ be a scheme. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scheme $X$ is Jacobson.
\item The scheme $X$ is ``locally Jacobson'' in the sense of
Definition \ref{definition-locally-P}.
\item For every affine open $U \subset X$ the ring $\mathcal{O}_X(U)$
is Jacobson.
\item There exists an affine open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ such that
each $\mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is Jacobson.
\item There exists an open covering $X = \bigcup X_j$
such that each open subscheme $X_j$ is Jacobson.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if $X$ is Jacobson then every open subscheme
is Jacobson.
